key_idea: Model the state as (robot cell, number of original commands consumed); executing the next command costs 0, deleting it costs 1, inserting any of the four moves costs 1, so the answer is a 0-1 shortest path to the exit cell.
sketch: There are at most 50*50*51 states. From (cell, i): with i < |s|, go to (move(cell, s[i]), i+1) at cost 0 or (cell, i+1) at cost 1 (delete); for each of the 4 directions go to (move(cell, d), i) at cost 1 (insert). A move into an obstacle or off the grid leaves the cell unchanged. Run 0-1 BFS with a deque from (start, 0) and output the distance of the first popped state standing on E, for any i, since the robot stops as soon as it reaches the exit and the remaining commands are irrelevant. Complexity O(r*c*|s|). Pitfall: the answer is not restricted to i = |s|, and blocked commands are ignored rather than invalid.
